title: Healthcare Needs and Illness Experience in Children With Rare Genetic and Metabolic Diseases
official: Healthcare Needs and Illness Experience in Children With Rare Genetic and Metabolic Diseases
summary:
This prospective observational study aims to describe and characterize the multidimensional care needs of children and adolescents aged 1 month to 18 years with rare genetic and metabolic diseases, with particular emphasis on the identification of pediatric palliative care needs.

The study seeks to answer the question of which clinical, physical, psychological, social, and care-related needs characterize this population, and to what extent these needs are associated with complex care requirements and potential eligibility for pediatric palliative care.

Additional objectives include assessing pain, sleep disturbances, psychological well-being, quality of life, physical and social functioning, medication-related adverse events, symptom interference with daily life, and caregiver burden. The study will also explore individual care needs and the transition from pediatric to adult healthcare services.

A subgroup of approximately 150 participants will undergo longitudinal assessments every three months for up to 12 months to describe changes in care needs over time and identify factors potentially associated with worsening clinical and care complexity. Furthermore, a qualitative substudy involving caregivers and adolescents will explore the lived experience of illness and the meaning attributed to the disease by children and their families through semi-structured interviews.

Overall, the study aims to provide a comprehensive understanding of the care needs and illness experience of children with rare genetic and metabolic diseases, supporting the early identification of complex needs and the development of more personalized, proactive, and family-centered care pathways.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Participants aged between 1 month and 18 years.
* Diagnosis of a rare genetic or metabolic disease.
* Written informed consent freely provided by the parents and/or legal guardians and obtained before study participation.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Diagnosis of trisomy 21 (Down syndrome).
* Unavailability of cultural mediators or language interpreters during the information and informed consent process, as well as during the assessment of patients or caregivers with limited or no understanding of the Italian language.
